analysis: The PR changes one documentation line in docs/architecture/inference.md (around line 1620, the gpt_oss row of the model_type table). The row now says a bf16 checkpoint keeps bf16 activations and native K/V on every layer, because the expert SwiGLU clamps with scalar bounds that take the activation dtype. The supplied units are only the base text of lines 1-796. They do not include the changed hunk, and the patch excerpt carries no code. No source, config, key handling, attestation, coordinator protocol, prefix-cache or SSD tier logic is modified. The documented behavior (dtype handling in GPTOSS+Experts.swift) is a numerical/correctness property, not a security control. It has no bearing on T-041 (prefix-cache cross-tenant oracle, HMAC-keyed SSD names, TTL, scope), A-001, TB-002, TB-007 or the attestation boundaries. The doc does not widen or contradict any threat-model mitigation. Remaining unverified contract: whether GPTOSS+Experts.swift actually behaves as the new row claims is outside the supplied evidence. That would be a correctness question, not a security conclusion. The unchanged base text on Nemotron Super prefix-cache scoping, 8 MiB media bounds and admission was read as context only and is not altered by this PR.
